_note: Operator reference data. Trade-body membership changes; the rejection letter always names the correct appeal route (POPLA for BPA operators, IAS for IPC operators), so this file is for context and drafting hints only. Edit freely — no code changes needed.

operators.name: APCOA Parking UK
operators.siteType: Railway stations and airports
themes: Station and airport sites are usually byelaw or contractual — check which basis the notice states.
Drop-off zones rely on very short periods; request the exact entry and exit timestamps.
Ask for the contractual terms incorporated at the point of entry.

operators.name: Britannia Parking Group Ltd
operators.siteType: Retail parks, town centres and hotel car parks
themes: BPA operator, so a rejection should include a POPLA code — check that it does, and that the code is valid.
Ask for the signage photographs taken at the time of the alleged contravention, not generic images of the site.
Check whether the charge was issued in the operator's own name and whether the landowner contract permits it.

operators.name: Civil Enforcement Ltd
operators.siteType: Retail and residential
themes: Confirm the land is 'relevant land' for POFA purposes — not all sites qualify.
Check the prescribed POFA wording is present in full on the Notice to Keeper.
Request proof of the operator's authority to issue charges in its own name.

operators.name: CP Plus Ltd
operators.siteType: Motorway services, retail and hospital car parks (trading as GroupNexus)
themes: Trades as GroupNexus, so the name on the notice and the name on the website rarely match. Appeal to whichever is printed, quoting the PCN reference exactly.
Motorway services sites turn on the free-parking period and the grace period that follows it — both are set by the site, not by statute.
As a BPA operator, a rejected appeal must come with a POPLA code. Write the code down when the rejection arrives; the window to use it is short.

operators.name: District Enforcement Ltd
operators.siteType: Residential estates, universities and retail parks
themes: IPC member: the escalation route is the IAS, not POPLA.
Residential sites usually turn on whether the keeper was ever shown the terms, and whether the landowner authorised charges.
Windscreen tickets followed by a postal notice must meet the 28-to-56-day POFA window, not the 14-day one.

operators.name: Euro Car Parks
operators.siteType: Retail, leisure and town-centre car parks
themes: Signage at the entrance is frequently the decisive point — request the site plan and dated photographs.
Confirm whether the charge was issued on the basis of a windscreen ticket or ANPR, as the POFA deadline differs.
Landowner authority is worth requesting where the site changed management.

operators.name: Excel Parking Services Ltd
operators.siteType: Retail and urban car parks
themes: IPC operators must offer the Independent Appeals Service (IAS) rather than POPLA — check the wording on the rejection.
Payment-machine faults and unclear tariff boards are common grounds.
Request the signage schedule and the machine maintenance log for the date in question.

operators.name: Highview Parking Ltd
operators.siteType: Retail and leisure car parks
themes: Part of the GroupNexus group, alongside CP Plus. Correspondence may come under any of those names.
ANPR sites: timestamps to the second decide most of these cases, so ask for both images and the camera identifiers.
A rejected appeal must offer POPLA. No code in the rejection is itself worth raising.

operators.name: Horizon Parking
operators.siteType: Retail, healthcare and education
themes: Healthcare and education sites often have permit schemes with unclear signage.
Request the evidence that the permit terms were brought to the driver's attention.
Check the notice date against the 14-day POFA window where no windscreen ticket was issued.

operators.name: Initial Parking Ltd
operators.siteType: Retail parks and town-centre car parks
themes: ANPR sites: request both entry and exit images, uncropped, and check the timestamps against the maximum stay.
The grace period at the end of a stay is a common ground — the BPA code expects time to leave after the permitted period.
Confirm the Notice to Keeper arrived within 14 days of the parking event if they want to hold the keeper liable.

operators.name: MET Parking Services Ltd
operators.siteType: Retail parks, hotels and airports
themes: Airport and hotel sites often hinge on the exact terms shown at entry.
Check the period of parking stated on the notice against the timestamps you are given.
Consider whether the charge is a genuine estimate of loss or a penalty, given ParkingEye v Beavis.

operators.name: Minster Baywatch Ltd
operators.siteType: Retail, leisure and residential car parks
themes: BPA operator: escalate a rejection to POPLA using the code in the rejection letter.
Residential and permit sites often turn on landowner authority and on whether the terms were communicated to the keeper.
Ask for the full evidence pack, including the signage plan, rather than the photographs they choose to send.

operators.name: NCP (National Car Parks)
operators.siteType: Pay-and-display, station and town-centre car parks
themes: Failure to display or a faulty machine is worth documenting with a timestamped photograph.
Check whether a valid ticket was purchased but misread — payment records can be requested.
Grace periods after paid time expires are commonly the winning point.

operators.name: Park Direct UK Ltd
operators.siteType: Retail and commercial car parks
themes: BPA operator: escalate a rejection to POPLA.
Ask for the evidence pack, including the signage plan and landowner authority.
Check the Notice to Keeper dates against POFA before arguing anything else.

operators.name: Parking & Enforcement Agency Ltd
operators.siteType: Retail and commercial car parks
themes: BPA member, so the independent stage is POPLA.
Smaller operators are more likely to have gaps in the Notice to Keeper timing — check the dates carefully.
Ask them to prove the landowner authorised charges in their own name at this specific site.

operators.name: ParkingEye Ltd
operators.siteType: ANPR camera, retail and motorway services
themes: Cases usually rest entirely on ANPR entry and exit stills, so ask for full-colour images and the second-by-second timestamps.
Check the Notice to Keeper against the 14-day POFA limit — pure ANPR cases have no windscreen ticket to extend it.
Maximum-stay sites often turn on whether the consideration period was enough to read the terms and park.

operators.name: ParkMaven Ltd
operators.siteType: Retail, leisure and residential car parks
themes: BPA operator: a rejected appeal should come with a POPLA code.
Screen-ticket and ANPR sites differ in the POFA timing that applies — check which one you are dealing with before arguing timing.
Signage clarity is the ground that most often succeeds at sites like these.

operators.name: Premier Park Ltd
operators.siteType: Retail, leisure and residential car parks
themes: BPA member, so escalate a rejection to POPLA with the code provided.
Ask for the landowner authority and the signage plan for the specific site.
Check the Notice to Keeper meets the 14-day POFA deadline if they seek to hold the keeper liable.

operators.name: Premier Parking Enforcement Ltd
operators.siteType: Retail, leisure and residential car parks
themes: BPA operator: the independent stage is POPLA.
Distinct from Premier Park Ltd despite the similar name — use the exact company named on your notice.
Signage, grace periods and POFA timing are the usual deciding points.

operators.name: Q-Park Ltd
operators.siteType: Town-centre and station multi-storey car parks
themes: BPA member, so a rejection escalates to POPLA.
Barrier and payment records matter here: ask for the entry and exit times and the payment record together.
If you paid but overstayed, the argument is about the grace period and the proportionality of the charge, not about whether you paid.

operators.name: Saba Park Solutions UK Ltd
operators.siteType: Station, hospital and town-centre car parks
themes: BPA operator: POPLA is the independent stage after a rejection.
Station and hospital sites often have complex tariff structures — ask for the tariff in force on the day.
Payment machine or app records are worth requesting: their failure is not your liability.

operators.name: SiP Parking Ltd
operators.siteType: Retail, leisure and residential car parks
themes: IPC member, so a rejected appeal escalates to the IAS rather than POPLA. The IAS window is shorter — do not sit on the rejection.
Operates under several trading names. Use the name on the notice and keep the reference exactly as printed.
Signage and the clarity of the terms are the strongest grounds at IPC sites, because the IAS decides on the balance of the evidence shown.

operators.name: Smart Parking Ltd
operators.siteType: Retail and leisure, ANPR
themes: ANPR-only evidence: presence at the cameras is not automatically a period of parking.
A second visit on the same day is a common cause of an apparently excessive recorded stay.
Ask for the full evidence pack before you accept the recorded duration.

operators.name: Spring Parking Ltd
operators.siteType: Retail and leisure car parks
themes: BPA operator, so POPLA is the route after a rejection.
Request the ANPR images and timestamps to the second, plus the signage photographs from the day.
Check the charge is pursued in the right name and that the landowner authorised it.

operators.name: Total Car Parks Ltd
operators.siteType: Retail, leisure and residential car parks
themes: Ask for the landowner authority. Smaller operators frequently issue charges on land where their contract does not clearly let them do so in their own name.
Signage is the usual weak point: look at whether the terms were visible on the way in, not just deeper into the site.
Check the Notice to Keeper date against the parking date — the 14-day POFA deadline catches operators of this size often.

operators.name: Total Parking Solutions Ltd
operators.siteType: Retail, leisure and commercial car parks
themes: BPA member: POPLA is the independent stage.
Distinct from Total Car Parks Ltd — check which company is named on the notice.
The POFA Notice to Keeper timing and the clarity of signage are the usual grounds.

operators.name: UK Car Park Management Ltd
operators.siteType: Residential estates and retail car parks
themes: BPA member: escalate to POPLA after a rejection.
Residential permit schemes frequently fail on whether the keeper was ever shown the terms.
Ask for the landowner contract — authority to issue charges in their own name is often the weakest link.

operators.name: UK Parking Control Ltd
operators.siteType: Residential, retail and industrial estates
themes: Often a windscreen ticket followed by a postal notice, so the 28-to-56-day POFA window applies, not the 14-day one.
Residential sites frequently turn on whether the keeper was ever shown the terms in the tenancy or lease.
Request the landowner contract where the operator's authority is not obvious.

operators.name: UKCPS Ltd
operators.siteType: Residential estates and retail car parks
themes: IPC member: a rejected appeal escalates to the IAS, not POPLA.
The IAS window after a rejection is short, so act as soon as the rejection arrives.
With IPC cases the evidence matters more — submit everything at the first attempt, because there is no second chance to add it.
